title: The fictional organization you will work with
body: All facts belong to the simulation. Some unknowns are deliberate: ask for them rather than assuming.

table.caption: Capstone scenario inputs
head: ID
Category
Fictional input
Evidence class
How to use it
rows: An unnamed fictional knowledge-work organization with 2,000 employees; Operations seeks better support throughput and Sales seeks better meeting readiness.
Use no real customer name, logo or live confidential data.
COO wants improved support capacity while maintaining quality this quarter; CRO wants more consistent preparation. Sponsor asks for a decision-ready value case, not a general AI experiment.
Draft separate outcome hypotheses; do not automatically combine overlapping value.
COO is the simulated executive sponsor; Support Operations owns the first metric; a technical champion coordinates platform owners; procurement/signature process is not yet known.
Map sponsor, champion, metric/data owner and procurement gap.

Support uses an ITSM platform, an approved knowledge repository and collaboration messages. Sales uses CRM, meeting notes and knowledge documents. Current connector/permission behavior has not been verified.
Do not infer product connector support or data access from generic system labels.
Support workflow scope: 200 potential users, two events per active user per workday, 240 workdays/year. These are supplied training assumptions, not measured deployment data.
Adoption is separate from addressable population.
Read case 2 min; find approved guidance 8 min; consult colleague 3 min; draft response 5 min; review/send 2 min. All durations are interview estimates of active work, not measured baselines.
Total map is 20 active min; model only the 8-min avoidable knowledge-friction burden in ROI Lab, not all 20.
Some cases wait one business day for specialist input; no frequency or monetary impact is known.
Keep elapsed delay separate; do not monetize as a day of labor saved.
Grounded access to approved guidance may reduce search friction and support drafting. Human source review, final response approval and escalation remain. Exact future timing is unknown.
Use a validation test and do not claim guaranteed automation.
Adoption 50%; avoidable burden 8 min/event; removable fraction 60%; relevant coverage 80%; recapture 25%; loaded rate $60/hour; risk haircut 10%; first-year all-in cost $30,000.
These factors illustrate explicit modeling, not approved Glean defaults/pricing or actual benefits.
Support manager proposes redeploying freed capacity toward backlog reduction. No headcount reduction, cancelled spend or avoided hire has been approved.
Classify benefits as directional capacity, not cash savings.

100 potential users; prepare for a customer meeting by reviewing CRM 10 min, finding notes 10 min, locating relevant content 15 min and drafting brief 10 min. Frequency and comparable baseline sample are unknown.
Second workflow map; no monetization until frequency/adoption/overlap are validated.
Autonomous refund approval, perfect cross-system BI joins and a custom legacy-source agent are requested. Authorization, deterministic data path and custom connector feasibility are unverified.
Park or phase based on effort and risk; ask diagnostic questions.
No standardized pre-rollout timing sample or system-outcome comparison exists. Support owner can arrange a sample but has not agreed dates or targets.
Propose cohort, period, metric definition, quality guardrail and owner.
The sponsor asks: Why not just give us a pilot? How does saved time turn into a business result? What evidence will replace estimates?
Demonstrate value, validation and objection-handling judgment.
Prepare A01–A20 as applicable, including first-wave use case log/matrix, two current/future map pairs, three-scenario model, metric cards, readout, recommendation, MAP, recap and handoff.
One versioned submission manifest; 8–10-minute executive readout plus short facilitation segment.
Online: recorded segment and submitted artifacts. In person: same artifacts and live observations. Use the same rubric, thresholds and critical gates.
Accept accessible written/live alternative as appropriate without removing the competence requirement.
